edits.name: The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture for paths: does every path $P_t$ have the Erdős-Hajnal property?
edits.field: Graph theory; induced subgraphs, Erdős-Hajnal conjecture
edits.statement: A graph $H$ has the Erdős-Hajnal property if there is $c=c(H)>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$ contains a clique or a stable set of size at least $n^{c}$. Erdős and Hajnal conjectured in 1977 that every graph $H$ has this property; the conjecture is open in general. This entry records the case of paths: does the path $P_t$ on $t$ vertices have the Erdős-Hajnal property for every $t\ge1$? Before this work it was known for $t\le5$ ($P_5$ by Nguyen, Scott and Seymour, 2023), and for all $t$ only with the weaker bound $2^{(\log n)^{1-o(1)}}$ in place of $n^{c}$.
edits.posedBy: Paul Erdős and András Hajnal (the general conjecture; paths are its special case)
edits.ageNote: The conjecture is from Erdős and Hajnal (1977, journal version 1989). The smallest open case for decades was $P_5$, settled by Nguyen, Scott and Seymour (arXiv 2312.15333, 2023); the same authors proved the near-Erdős-Hajnal property for every path. The general conjecture remains open.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2610.24887 (Tung H. Nguyen, v1 17 October 2026): $P_t$ has the Erdős-Hajnal property for every $t$. Theorem 1.2 extends it to the trees $S_{1,2,t}$ and the graphs $S'_{1,2,t}$, which include the bull, E and the bird. This is not the general conjecture. Concurrent independent proofs of the path case: Yuwen Zhou's repository (public 8 October 2026, with a Lean development conditional on stated literature hypotheses and an anonymous $P_6$ project), later arXiv:2611.01963 (Huang, Zhou, Zhou; Claude Opus 5.5 and ChatGPT-6), and Google DeepMind's Cogentic manuscript with Lean (18 October). The first public proof of the path case may not be this one.
edits.aiRole: From the paper's Declaration of generative AI use: ChatGPT-6 Astra was mathematically involved in two subsections and one section; the ideas in the rest are the author's. Asked to prove a weaker version of a modular-decomposition lemma, Astra proved the full purity version; after discussions directed by the author it found the proof of the path-splitting lemma for $r=5$, which the author extended to general $r$; it also cleaned up the author's endpoint-switching argument. Astra assisted with proofreading and mathematical review; ChatGPT-6 Luna helped copy-edit and ChatGPT-6 Sol drew the figures.

The proof (39 pages) was not refereed here and there is no formal proof of this paper. Checked against the concurrent work: Zhou's GitHub repository was created 8 October 2026 (UTC), Nguyen's v1 posted 17 October, DeepMind's manuscript committed 18 October; DeepMind's README credits Nguyen as first to their knowledge. The catalog had no entry on this question.
edits.significanceNote: The Erdos-Hajnal conjecture is one of the central open problems of structural graph theory, and paths were its most-watched open family: the five-vertex path alone resisted for decades. Not the full conjecture, so well below Sidorenko's conjecture (52), a whole conjecture in extremal graph theory. Level with the power saving for planar halving lines (42), below the planar and bounded-treewidth GNRS cases (45), and well above the Erdos-Hajnal high-girth subgraph question (25).

edits.name: Haagerup's problem on decomposable maps: does $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ on $\ell_\infty^3$ force injectivity?
edits.field: Operator algebras; completely bounded and decomposable maps
edits.statement: For $C^*$-algebras $A,B$, Haagerup introduced the decomposable norm $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}$ on linear combinations of completely positive maps $A\to B$, with $\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}\le\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}$, and proved that a von Neumann algebra $N$ is injective if $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for every $n$ and every linear map $T:\ell_\infty^n\to N$. For $n=2$ the two norms always coincide. Haagerup's Problem 3.8: let $N$ be a von Neumann algebra such that $\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}$ for every linear map $T:\ell_\infty^3\to N$. Is $N$ injective?
edits.posedBy: Uffe Haagerup, Injectivity and decomposition of completely bounded maps, Lecture Notes in Math. 1132 (1985), Problem 3.8
edits.ageNote: Posed in Haagerup's contribution to the Buşteni conference of 1983, published 1985. Pisier's 2020 book (Remark 23.4) records it as open, with two known cases: $N$ with a cyclic vector and $N'$ generated by two unitaries, and (Junge and Le Merdy, 1999) when the condition holds for all matrix algebras $M_k(N)$.
edits.resultNote: Yes: every von Neumann algebra $N$ with $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for all linear $T:\ell_\infty^3\to N$ is injective, so $N$ is injective if and only if the two norms agree on maps from $\ell_\infty^3$. The proof does not use the September 2026 OpenAI claim on the generator problem; the paper remarks that granting it shortens the proof.
edits.aiRole: From the paper's AI statement: "This work was carried out in collaboration with an AI system (Claude Opus 5.5). The main argument was developed in discussions between the author and the AI system, and the manuscript was drafted mainly by the AI system. The author has verified all proofs and takes full responsibility for the content of this paper."

Level with the near-inclusions embedding question (20), below Marrakchi's relative bicentralizer conjecture (32), and far below the generator problem (50) and Kadison's similarity problem (58), which the whole field knows.

edits.name: Petz's conjecture: the scalar curvature of the Kubo-Mori metric increases as a state becomes more mixed
edits.statement: On invertible $n\times n$ density matrices, call $\rho_1$ more mixed than $\rho_2$ if for each $k$ the sum of the $k$ largest eigenvalues of $\rho_1$ is at most that of $\rho_2$. Petz conjectured that the scalar curvature of the Kubo-Mori (Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori) metric is monotone under this order: $\mathrm{Scal}(\rho_1)\ge\mathrm{Scal}(\rho_2)$ whenever $\rho_1$ is more mixed than $\rho_2$. In particular the maximum would be at the maximally mixed state.
edits.posedBy: Dénes Petz, Geometry of canonical correlation on the state space of a quantum system, J. Math. Phys. 35 (1994)
edits.ageNote: Dittmann (arXiv 1999, Linear Algebra Appl. 2000) reduced the conjecture to an Assertion, the concavity of an explicit symmetric function $h$ on $(0,\infty)^3$, supported by millions of numerical tests but unproved. Andai (2003) proved monotonicity of part of the curvature; Gibilisco and Isola (2005) posed a stronger conjecture on Wigner-Yanase-Dyson metrics.
edits.resultNote: Proves Dittmann's Assertion: $h$ extends real-analytically to $(0,\infty)^3$ and is strictly concave, $h(\lambda X+(1-\lambda)Y)>\lambda h(X)+(1-\lambda)h(Y)$ for distinct $X,Y$ and $0<\lambda<1$. With Dittmann's Theorem 3, used as published, this gives Petz's conjecture. The key step writes $h=-1/(8M)$ with $M$ homogeneous of degree one and shows $t\mapsto1/M(X+tY)$ is a Stieltjes function.
edits.aiRole: From the Hexagon provenance statement: "The results in this paper were developed with an AI assistant (OpenAI's GPT Pro). None of the claims were obtained zero-shot: they emerged through sustained back-and-forth discussion, including failed attempts, counterexamples, audits, and repairs." Hexagon labels the text a mix of human-written and AI-generated, with human understanding of all parts.
edits.verificationNote: Read by this site on 15 November 2026: the Hexagon record and PDF (hexagon:2610.00717v1) and the author's timestamped repository (v1 committed 9 October 2026). An independent check written here found the concavity inequality satisfied on 20,000 random triples of points and weights at 60-digit precision, which supports but does not prove it. The proof itself was not refereed, and Dittmann's Theorem 3 is used as published. No expert reaction found.
edits.significanceNote: A thirty-year-old conjecture of Petz, reduced by Dittmann in 2000 to one concavity statement nobody could prove, known to the quantum information geometry community but not beyond it. Level with the Yun-Sra-Jadbabaie shuffling inequalities and the Zhu-Fang-Shi invariant projection question (both 15), below the inverse generator problem (22), above the Kreiss constants separation (12).

edits.name: Equality of the Mirković-Vilonen and theta bases (Kamnitzer's conjecture)
edits.statement: Let $G$ be a connected complex semisimple group and $N$ a maximal unipotent subgroup. $\mathbb{C}[N]$ carries the Mirković-Vilonen (MV) basis, from MV cycles in the affine Grassmannian via geometric Satake (Baumann-Kamnitzer-Knutson), and the theta basis of Gross-Hacking-Keel-Kontsevich for its cluster structure. Kamnitzer's ICM 2022 report closes its cluster-algebra section with the conjecture: the MV and theta bases for $\mathbb{C}[N]$ coincide. Do they?
edits.posedBy: Joel Kamnitzer, Perfect bases in representation theory: three mountains and their springs, Proc. ICM 2022 (arXiv 2201.02289)
edits.ageNote: Stated in the ICM 2022 report (arXiv January 2022), where Kamnitzer calls it a wild conjecture supported by three pieces of weak evidence. The same section asks whether the theta basis is biperfect and conjectures that the MV basis contains all cluster monomials.
edits.aiRole: From the paper's 'AI use and scholarly credit' section: the initial draft was developed through seven ChatGPT-6-Pro conversations (about 23 hours), with four hours of research using Pharos, then polished with Codex and reviewed by Rethlas-OSV. That review found an error invalidating the main proof; ChatGPT-6-Pro was asked to spend six hours repairing it, a separate ChatGPT conversation reviewed the repair, and Codex expanded the manuscript from 21 to 52 pages. A second Rethlas-OSV review found further errors, one again blocking the proof as written, with corrections supplied; after these the manuscript passed. Hexagon labels the work 'a mix of human-written and AI-generated text', human understanding 'some parts'. The author does not claim priority or ownership of the results.
edits.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here on 15 November 2026: the Hexagon record and PDF (hexagon 2611.00006v1, 52 pages), its AI-use section, the introduction and the statement of Theorem 17.1, read against the TeX source of Kamnitzer's ICM report (arXiv 2201.02289v2), whose conjecture reads 'The MV and theta bases for $\mathbb{C}[N]$ coincide'. The statement matches; the paper cites it as Conjecture 6.9. The proof itself was not read or refereed. By the paper's own account the argument was drafted by ChatGPT-6-Pro and twice repaired after AI review found errors blocking the main theorem, and Hexagon records human understanding as 'some parts'. Hexagon is a moderated but not peer-reviewed repository. No earlier claim was found in this catalog or in an arXiv API search. Resolution is Candidate until someone independent checks the argument in public.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 17.1: for every connected complex semisimple group $G$, the normalized MV basis of $\mathbb{C}[N]$ equals the regular theta basis. The bases are paired by weight and leading data; MV structure constants come from spatial fusion in the Beilinson-Drinfeld Grassmannian (Baumann-Kamnitzer-Knutson) and theta structure constants from punctured logarithmic curve counts on an affine Richardson variety, and the two are shown to agree, so the multiplicative pairing is the identity. Caveats: AI-drafted and AI-repaired proof, no independent expert review, author disclaims priority.
edits.significanceNote: A four-year-old conjecture from an ICM report, central to how geometric (MV) and cluster (theta) bases of the unipotent coordinate ring relate, but known mainly within geometric representation theory and offered by its author as a wild guess on weak evidence. Placed below the equivariant Hikita conjecture for quivers (30), a better-circulated conjecture in the same circle, level with the periodicity conjecture for finite-dimensional algebras (25), above the type D saturation conjecture (20).

edits.name: Bermond's lobster conjecture for lobsters of maximum degree three
edits.statement: Bermond (1979) conjectured that every lobster is graceful. A lobster is a finite tree in which every vertex lies within distance two of a single path. A tree on $n$ vertices is graceful if its vertices can be labelled with the distinct integers $0,1,\dots,n-1$ so that the $n-1$ edge differences $|f(u)-f(v)|$ are exactly $1,2,\dots,n-1$. Is every lobster graceful?
edits.posedBy: Jean-Claude Bermond, Graceful graphs, radio antennae and French windmills (Graph Theory and Combinatorics, Pitman, 1979)
edits.resultNote: Every finite lobster of maximum degree at most three is graceful: its vertex labels can be taken to be $0,\dots,n-1$ with edge differences exactly $1,\dots,n-1$. The proof decomposes the lobster along a maximal witnessing path into spine cells and assembles labels from a finite certificate of 6,104 local rules, checked in Lean. The unrestricted lobster conjecture remains open. Related earlier work: Luiz, Campos and Richter (2019) give alpha-labelings for maximum-degree-three lobsters under extra restrictions on legs and endings.

The headline theorem Lobster.every_subcubic_lobster_is_graceful was read: for a finite simple graph that is a tree, has maximum degree at most 3 and has a simple path within graph distance 2 of every vertex, it gives a bijection of vertices onto $0,\dots,n-1$ and a bijection of edges onto differences $1,\dots,n-1$, with $|f(u)-f(v)|$ on every edge. That matches the conjecture restricted to maximum degree three. A grep found no sorry, admit, axiom or unsafe; three finite checks use native_decide, so the proof trusts Lean's compiler for those evaluations. The rule table has 6,104 rows and its SHA-256 matches the README. Not rebuilt here. The statement is not independently anchored.

edits.name: Optimality of the D4 lattice quantizer in dimension four
edits.statement: Is the root lattice $D_4$ the optimal lattice quantizer in dimension four, that is, does it minimize the normalized second moment $G(L)=\frac{1}{4\,\mathrm{covol}(L)^{3/2}}\int_{V(L)}\|x\|^2\,dx$ of the Voronoi cell $V(L)$ among all lattices $L\subset\mathbb{R}^4$? Gersho (1979) proposed the $D_4$ structure; Barnes and Sloane (1983) proved the body-centred cubic lattice optimal in dimension three, and no optimal lattice quantizer had been proved in any higher dimension.

edits.name: The Díaz-Park sharpness conjecture for saturated fusion systems
edits.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a saturated fusion system over a finite $p$-group $S$, and let $M=(M^*,M_*)$ be a Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over $\mathbb F_p$ (in the sense of Díaz and Park) with finite-dimensional values. Díaz and Park conjectured that the higher limits of $M^*$ over the orbit category of $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups vanish: $\varprojlim^i_{\mathcal O(\mathcal F^c)} M^*=0$ for all $i>0$. Its cohomological case, sharpness of the subgroup decomposition of every $p$-local finite group, is a question in the open-problem list of Aschbacher, Kessar and Oliver (2011) and the sharpness conjecture of Aschbacher and Oliver (2016). Is the conjecture true for every saturated fusion system?
edits.posedBy: Antonio Díaz and Sejong Park, Mackey functors and sharpness for fusion systems, Homology Homotopy Appl. 17 (2015); cohomological case: Aschbacher, Kessar and Oliver (2011), Section III.7
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor $M$ for $\mathcal F$ over $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$, $\varprojlim^i_{\mathcal O(\mathcal F^c)}M^*=0$ for all $i>0$; this also holds over any field of characteristic $p$, which contains the conjecture. Corollary 1.2: the subgroup decomposition (and Libman's normaliser decomposition) of every $p$-local finite group over the centric subgroups is sharp, answering the Aschbacher-Kessar-Oliver question. The proof is algebraic and does not use the classification of finite simple groups. Earlier cases: finite groups and abelian index-$p$ subgroups (Díaz-Park), $n\le p-2$ (Glauberman-Lynd), punctured groups (Henke-Libman-Lynd), $\mathrm G_2(p)$ (Grazian-Marmo).

edits.name: Rosenthal-Yuen question: unitaryQIP = unitaryPSPACE
edits.statement: Rosenthal and Yuen introduced the unitary synthesis classes $\mathsf{unitaryQIP}$ (unitaries synthesizable by a polynomial-time quantum verifier interacting with an untrusted prover) and $\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ (unitaries implementable in polynomial space), and left both inclusions open: is every $\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ family in $\mathsf{unitaryQIP}$ with nontrivial completeness and soundness, and is every $\mathsf{unitaryQIP}$ family implementable by space-uniform circuits? Does $\mathsf{unitaryQIP}=\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$, the unitary analogue of $\mathsf{QIP}=\mathsf{PSPACE}$ and $\mathsf{stateQIP}=\mathsf{statePSPACE}$?
edits.posedBy: Gregory Rosenthal and Henry Yuen, Interactive proofs for synthesizing quantum states and unitaries (arXiv 2108.07192; ITCS 2022), open problems
edits.ageNote: Posed in August 2021. Rosenthal and Yuen proved the polynomial-action case; Metger and Yuen (FOCS 2023) proved stateQIP = statePSPACE; Bostanci et al. (ITCS 2026) proved the average-case analogue avgUnitaryQIP = avgUnitaryPSPACE.

edits.name: Morel's purity conjecture for $\mathbb A^1$-homotopy sheaves of pure $S^1$-spectra
edits.statement: Let $S$ be a separated noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension. Call an $S^1$-spectrum over $S$ pure if it lies in the smallest triangulated subcategory of the stable $\mathbb A^1$-homotopy category containing the suspension spectra of smooth projective $S$-schemes and closed under arbitrary coproducts and retracts; call a Nisnevich sheaf on $\mathrm{Sm}_S$ pure if Zariski and Nisnevich cohomology agree and cohomology is insensitive, in a range of degrees, to removing closed subsets of high codimension. Morel conjectured (Conjecture 6.4.12) that for every pure $S^1$-spectrum $E$ and every $n$, the sheaf $\underline{\pi}^{\mathbb A^1}_n(E)$ is pure. Is this true?
edits.posedBy: Fabien Morel, The stable A1-connectivity theorems, K-Theory 35 (2005), Conjecture 6.4.12
edits.resultNote: Disproof claimed. Theorem A: over a regular base $S$, $K_S\wedge M$ is pure for every spectrum $M$. Theorem B: injectivity of restriction to dense opens for its homotopy sheaves is equivalent to Gersten injectivity at the henselized local rings of smooth $S$-schemes. Corollary D: with $A=\mathbb Z_3[[x,y]]/(3+x^2-y^3)$ and the author's earlier class in $K_2(A;\mathbb Z/3)$ that dies on the fraction field (arXiv 2608.05005), $\underline{\pi}^{\mathbb A^1}_2(K_S/3)(S)\to\underline{\pi}^{\mathbb A^1}_2(K_S/3)(U)$ is not injective, so the conjecture fails over $S=\mathrm{Spec}\,A$, and also over $\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb Z[1/2][x,y]/(3+x^2-y^3)$. Integral and rational failures are left conditional on unrefereed Gersten counterexamples.

edits.name: Deterministic integer factoring in time $N^{o(1)}$
edits.statement: Every deterministic integer factoring algorithm with a proved running time has had a fixed positive exponent: trial division $N^{1/2+o(1)}$, Lehman $N^{1/3+o(1)}$, Pollard and Strassen $N^{1/4+o(1)}$, Hittmeir $N^{2/9+o(1)}$, and Harvey's $N^{1/5+o(1)}$ (2021), improved only by logarithmic factors since. The rigorous subexponential methods (Dixon, Lenstra-Pomerance) are randomized, and the deterministic sieves rest on unproved heuristics. Is there one deterministic algorithm that factors every positive integer $N$ in time $N^{o(1)}$, that is, in time $O(N^{\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$?
edits.ageNote: No single source poses the N^o(1) form. It is the endpoint of the tracked deterministic exponent: 1/4 from Pollard (1974) and Strassen (1976) stood for about forty years, then 2/9 (Hittmeir) and 1/5 (Harvey 2021; Harvey-Hittmeir 2022). Harvey asks only whether 1/6 is reachable.
edits.aiRole: Per the paper and its Hexagon provenance statement, all the ideas were AI-generated: the reduction to counting divisors with prescribed leading bits, the choice of method (a re-proved part of the counting engine of Anthropic's 3-SAT preprint) and the whole 36,000-line Lean proof were produced by Claude Opus 5.5 agents, which also drafted the exposition. The two authors posed the questions, designed and audited the 13-line formal statement, and edited the text; they say they did not read the proof.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1 (in Lean): one deterministic Turing machine (Mathlib's TM2 model, every alphabet finite, input and output in binary) outputs the smallest prime factor of $N$ and, for every $k\ge1$, halts within $C_k2^{n/k}$ steps on $n$-bit inputs, so in time $2^{o(n)}=N^{o(1)}$. Theorem 2 (not in Lean, a few lines): applying it at most $\log_2N$ times gives the complete factorization in time $N^{o(1)}$. The algorithm is galactic and slower than the heuristic sieves; what is new is a proved deterministic $N^{o(1)}$ bound.

edits.name: The pure semisimplicity conjecture
edits.field: Ring theory; representation theory of rings
edits.statement: A ring $R$ is right pure semisimple if every right $R$-module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules. Every ring of finite representation type is both left and right pure semisimple. The pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts the converse from one side: every right pure semisimple ring is of finite representation type, equivalently every right pure semisimple ring is also left pure semisimple. It was known for commutative rings (Warfield), Artin algebras (Auslander) and rings with a polynomial identity (Herzog), and Herzog and Simson reduced it to hereditary triangular matrix rings over two division rings. Is it true?
edits.ageNote: Pure semisimple rings were defined by Simson (1977); the conjecture has been worked on since then by Simson, Herzog (1994), Garcia (2014, 2018) and Saroch (2021), among others. The paper does not name who first stated it, so posed-by is left blank.
edits.aiRole: From the paper's declaration of AI use (v1): GPT-6 Astra contributed to the exploration that led to the criterion used and to the proof of the main theorem, in particular the construction of the division rings $T$ and $H_r$. The author verified the proofs and completed the Lean 4 formalization and the editing with the assistance of GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. Version 2 adds Claude Fable 5.1 for the finite-order (Coxeter type) results, which are not part of this entry.
edits.resultNote: Over $\mathbb Q$ with $q=1/2$ (v1; in v2 any field element $q$ of infinite multiplicative order), quantum chains of division rings give an extension $H\subseteq T$ whose bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,\dots)$ and $\dim{}_HT=\infty$. The triangular ring $R=\begin{pmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{pmatrix}$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so the conjecture fails. Version 2 also gives pairwise Morita inequivalent counterexamples and hereditary artinian rings of every Coxeter type $\mathbb I_2(m)$, $m\ge4$.

edits.name: Mathieu's spectral isometry conjecture
edits.field: Operator algebras; preserver problems in Banach algebras
edits.statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be unital complex $C^*$-algebras. A linear map $T:A\to B$ is a spectral isometry if $r(Ta)=r(a)$ for every $a\in A$, where $r$ is the spectral radius. Mathieu conjectured that every unital surjective spectral isometry between unital $C^*$-algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, that is, a linear bijection with $T(a^2)=T(a)^2$ for all $a$. edits.name: Ulam's floating-body problem for origin-symmetric bodies
edits.statement: Ulam (Scottish Book, Problem 19) asked whether a convex body of uniform relative density $\rho\in(0,1)$ that floats in equilibrium in every orientation must be a Euclidean ball. Ryabogin (2022) answered this negatively with non-centrally-symmetric bodies of revolution at $\rho=\frac12$ in every dimension $d\ge3$. For origin-symmetric bodies the answer at $\rho=\frac12$ is yes (Schneider and Falconer in dimension 3; Florentin, Schütt, Werner and Zhang in all dimensions), and Ryabogin noted that no results were known for other densities. Must an origin-symmetric convex body in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge3$, that floats in equilibrium in every orientation at some density $\rho\neq\frac12$ be a ball?
edits.posedBy: Stanisław Ulam (Scottish Book, Problem 19); the origin-symmetric case at densities other than 1/2 stayed open after Schneider and Falconer
edits.ageNote: Scottish Book Problem 19, also in Ulam's A Collection of Mathematical Problems (1960). Schneider (1970) and Falconer (1983) settled the origin-symmetric case at density 1/2 in dimension 3; Florentin, Schütt, Werner and Zhang (PAMS 2022) in every dimension. Ryabogin (Ann. of Math. 2022) answered Ulam's question with non-symmetric bodies. Wegner (2009) gave formal symmetric branches in dimension 3.

GPT models working in Codex (Hexagon's provenance record names GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra) extended it to every dimension $d\ge3$ and completed the proof, and assisted with drafting, revising and proofreading. Hexagon labels the text 'a mix of human-written and AI-generated text', with human understanding of 'some parts'.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1 and Corollary 2: in every dimension $d\ge3$ there are nonspherical, origin-symmetric, strictly convex bodies of revolution with real-analytic boundary that float in equilibrium in every orientation. Their densities lie near the cap fraction of the unit ball at height $(d+4)^{-1/2}$ (about $0.230$ for $d=3$), and the same bodies float at the complementary density. The bodies exist on closed parameter sets of asymptotically full measure near an isolated degree-four resonance. Not addressed: dimension 2 (floating logs), and exactly which densities admit such bodies.
edits.verificationNote: Checked here on 15 November 2026. The Hexagon paper (2610.00629v1, de Groot and Price, 29 October 2026) was read through Theorem 1, Corollary 2 and Lemma 3, and its disclosure of AI contributions. The analytic part (small divisors via Matveev's bound, Newton iteration) was not checked. No Lean formalization.

edits.name: Is $\mathbb{Z}$ Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$?
edits.statement: Julia Robinson (1949) showed that $\mathbb Z$ is first-order definable in $\mathbb Q$, and Koenigsmann gave a universal definition, but whether an existential one exists remained open. Is there a polynomial $P\in\mathbb Z[x,y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ such that for every $x\in\mathbb Q$, $x\in\mathbb Z$ if and only if $P(x,y)=0$ for some $y\in\mathbb Q^m$? Mazur's 1992 conjecture on the topology of rational points predicts that no such $P$ exists; a positive answer would refute it and, with the Davis-Putnam-Robinson-Matiyasevich theorem, make Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb Q$ undecidable.

edits.name: The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
edits.field: Analysis of Boolean functions; quantum query complexity
edits.statement: Let $p:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R$ be a polynomial of degree $d$ with $0\le p(X)\le1$ for all $X\in\{0,1\}^N$ and $\mathbb E_X[(p(X)-\mathbb E[p])^2]\ge\varepsilon$, where $X$ is uniform on $\{0,1\}^N$. Aaronson and Ambainis conjectured that some variable $i$ has influence $\mathrm{Inf}_i[p]=\mathbb E_X[(p(X)-p(X^i))^2]\ge(\varepsilon/d)^{O(1)}$, where $X^i$ is $X$ with bit $i$ flipped. They showed it implies that every $T$-query quantum algorithm can be simulated on most inputs by a classical algorithm with $\mathrm{poly}(T)$ queries, so exponential quantum speedups need structured inputs. Is the conjecture true?
edits.posedBy: Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis
edits.ageNote: Conjecture 6 of arXiv:0911.0996 (2009), Conjecture 1.7 of Theory of Computing 10 (2014). Known before: Dinur-Friedgut-Kindler-O'Donnell gives the bound with exponential dependence on d; Montanaro proved a special case; Bhattacharya proved it for many random restrictions; Blanc, Docter, Strassle and Tan settled a bounded-round special case in 2026.

A model instance packaged the results into a first draft, which Turturean reviewed, edited and takes responsibility for. The Lean formalization was also produced by AI models.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: every $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ of degree at most $d\ge1$ has a coordinate $j$ with $\mathrm{Inf}_j(f)\ge\frac{\sqrt{15}}{500\pi^4}\,\mathrm{Var}(f)^{5/2}/d^6$. In the conjecture's own normalisation this gives $\mathrm{Inf}_i[p]\ge(\varepsilon/d)^7$. Corollary: the acceptance probability of a $T$-query quantum algorithm can be approximated to within $\varepsilon$ on all but a $\delta$ fraction of inputs by a deterministic classical algorithm making at most $(4T)^8\varepsilon^{-14}\delta^{-8}$ queries. The proof combines fractional certificates (after Lovett and Zhang), an all-pairs inequality related to Reimer's butterfly lemma, and a row bound for bounded polynomials.

edits.statement: A sorting adversary answers the comparisons of a sorting algorithm online and is legal if every finite sequence of its answers is consistent with some total order. Atallah and Kosaraju (1981) gave an efficient deterministic adversary forcing every correct sorter to make $\frac12 n\log_2 n$ comparisons, and Kaplan, Zamir and Zwick (SODA 2019) raised this to $\frac{37}{64}n\log_2 n$. Does one exist?

edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: there is a deterministic legal adversary, initialized using only $n$, that uses polynomially many bit operations per query and forces every correct sorter to make at least $(1-o(1))n\log_2 n$ comparisons. edits.name: Free energy of the Hopfield model at every temperature and loading ratio
edits.statement: In the Hopfield model, $N$ spins $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^N$ interact through $M_N$ independent uniform $\pm1$ patterns $x^1,\ldots,x^{M_N}$, with free energy $F_N(\beta)=\frac1N\log\int\exp\big(\frac{\beta}{2N}|X_N^\top\sigma|^2\big)\,dP_N(\sigma)$. In the extensive-storage regime $M_N/N\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)$, Amit, Gutfreund and Sompolinsky derived a replica phase diagram (1985-1987), and rigorous results (Bovier, Gayrard, Picco; Pastur, Shcherbina, Tirozzi; Talagrand) covered only high temperature, small $\alpha$ with large $\beta$, or assumed concentration of the order parameters. Does $\lim_N \mathbb E F_N(\beta)$ exist for every $\alpha>0$ and $\beta>0$, and can it be identified by an explicit variational formula?
edits.ageNote: Open since the replica analysis of Amit, Gutfreund and Sompolinsky (1985-1987); the manuscript's related-work section surveys the partial rigorous results, including Talagrand's 1998 and 2000 papers and the Hopfield chapters of his Mean Field Models for Spin Glasses.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for Bernoulli patterns and every $\alpha,\beta>0$, $\lim_N\mathbb E F_N(\beta)=F(\alpha,\beta)$ exists and equals $\sup_{r>0,\,0\le h\le\beta}\inf_{\zeta\in\mathcal P_{<1}}\{\alpha\mathcal R(r)-\frac{h^2}{2\beta}+\mathscr P_{\alpha\beta r^2/2}(\zeta,h)+\alpha\mathcal E(\zeta)\}$, a Parisi-type formula; $F_N(\beta)$ also converges almost surely and in $L^1$. Proposition 1.2 gives a unique minimizing $\zeta$ for each $(r,h)$. Concurrent work, cited by the paper: Camilli, Contucci and Mingione (arXiv 2610.32618, 23 Oct 2026) gave a formula for Gaussian patterns, and Barra and Durante (arXiv 2610.41938, 30 Oct 2026) proved existence of the limit for Bernoulli patterns without identifying it.
edits.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. The abstracts of the two concurrent preprints it cites (Barra-Durante 2610.41938, Camilli-Contucci-Mingione 2610.32618) were read to place it. The proof was not read or refereed here.
edits.significanceNote: The free energy of the Hopfield model at positive loading and low temperature has been open since the replica predictions of the mid-1980s and is one of the classic problems of rigorous spin glass theory. edits.name: The $k$-Clique Hypothesis
edits.statement: Nesetril and Poljak (1985) reduced $k$-Clique in $n$-node graphs to triangle detection in $O(n^{k/3})$-node graphs, giving an $n^{\omega k/3+o(1)}$-time algorithm for $k$ divisible by 3, where $\omega$ is the exponent of square matrix multiplication. Woeginger (2004) challenged algorithm designers to beat this for some fixed $k$, and Abboud, Backurs and Vassilevska Williams formulated the $k$-Clique Hypothesis: in the word-RAM model with $O(\log n)$-bit words, for $k$ divisible by 3, detecting a $k$-clique in an $n$-node graph requires $n^{\omega k/3-o(1)}$ time. Many fine-grained lower bounds rest on it. Is it true?

edits.statement: In the matroid secretary problem of Babaioff, Immorlica and Kleinberg, the elements of a matroid $\mathcal{M}=(V,\mathcal{I})$ with $n=|V|$ carry nonnegative values that are revealed in uniformly random order. An online algorithm must accept or reject each element irrevocably on arrival, keeping the accepted set independent, and is $c$-competitive if its expected total value is at least $1/c$ times the maximum value of an independent set. Does every matroid admit an $O(1)$-competitive algorithm, with a universal constant independent of the matroid?

edits.name: The L'vov-Kaplansky conjecture
edits.statement: Let $K$ be a field and let $f\in K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_m\rangle$ be a multilinear noncommutative polynomial. Is the image $f(M_n(K)^m)=\{f(A_1,\ldots,A_m): A_i\in M_n(K)\}$ a vector subspace of $M_n(K)$ for every $n\ge1$?
edits.posedBy: I. V. L'vov, Dniester Notebook, Problem 1.98 (4th ed., Novosibirsk 1993); the question is also associated with Kaplansky
edits.aiRole: From the Hexagon record's provenance statement: "The main results were developed over ten GPT-6-Pro research runs with a combined scheduled duration of 62.5 hours. Codex was used to audit the proofs and polish the manuscript. A Rethlas-OSV review will be added in a later version." The record is labelled "A mix of human-written and AI-generated text" and "Human understanding: some parts". The PDF itself carries no AI statement.
edits.verificationNote: Read by this site on 15 November 2026. The source is a Hexagon deposit (hexagon:2611.00206v1, deposited 8 November, version 1 of 10 November) by Qiyue Tang, who is identified by ORCID with no affiliation; the record labels the text as mixed human and AI-written and the author's understanding as covering only some parts. Theorem 1.1 was read and matches the result note. The proof (33 pages) was not checked. A small computation written here over GF(7) for degrees 3 and 4 with n = d agreed in 80 of 80 random cases that the trace of f vanishes identically exactly when f is formally traceless, the elementary half of the dichotomy; the surjectivity for n at least B(d) was not tested, since B(d) is not explicit. No formalisation.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for each $d\ge2$ there is an integer $B(d)$ such that for every field $K$, every nonzero ordinary homogeneous multilinear polynomial $f$ of degree $d$ over $K$ and every $n\ge B(d)$, $f(\mathfrak{sl}_n(K)^d)=f(M_n(K)^d)$, and this image is $\mathfrak{sl}_n(K)$ if $f$ is formally traceless (every cyclic coefficient sum vanishes) and $M_n(K)$ otherwise. So the image is a vector space for all $n\ge B(d)$. $B(d)$ is not made explicit, and the orders $n<B(d)$ remain open.
edits.ageNote: The year is that of the Dniester Notebook edition the source cites. Known before: $n=2$ under a root-closure hypothesis (Kanel-Belov, Malev, Rowen 2012) and degree three over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero (Vitas, LAA 2026), as the paper's introduction records.
edits.significanceNote: A named conjecture in the theory of polynomial identities, with a steady literature and a survey of partial results, famous within ring theory but not beyond it. Placed level with Gersten's conjecture for integral K-theory at 30 and the complete Crouzeix conjecture at 30, below Rota's unimodality conjecture for matroid flats at 36. The entry is Partial, which the score does not discount.

edits.name: Pilz's Extended 1-2-3 Conjecture
edits.statement: For every finite nonempty set $A$ of positive integers and every $n\ge1$, is $|A\,\triangle\,2A\,\triangle\cdots\triangle\,nA|\ge n$? Equivalently, are there at least $n$ integers $m$ with an odd number of representations $m=aj$ with $a\in A$ and $1\le j\le n$?
edits.posedBy: G. F. Pilz, On polynomial near-ring codes (Contrib. Gen. Algebra 8, 1992); stated as a conjecture by Huang, Ke and Pilz (Proc. AMS 138, 2010)
edits.ageNote: Pilz (1992) proved it for $n\le6$ and found no counterexample by computer. The case $A=\{1,\dots,k\}$ was proved by Huang-Ke-Pilz and by Pach-Szabo (2008-09). Holdridge and Pach (arXiv 2607.00934, July 2026) proved it for $n\le8$ and for $n\ge2(3^{80}-321)$, leaving a finite but enormous range.
edits.verificationNote: Read by this site on 15 November 2026, not rebuilt. The headline theorem WeightedPilz.weighted_symmetric_difference states n <= |intervalSymmetricDifference n A| for every finite nonempty A of positive integers, where membership means lying in an odd number of the sets {a, 2a, ..., na}; that is Pilz's conjecture as posed. The check files reject any axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. GitHub Actions run 43065981090 on that commit built all three projects and ran the checks successfully. An exhaustive computation written here (all A within 1..16, n <= 10, plus 20,000 random cases) found no violation. The written proofs have not been checked by a human mathematician; the formal statement was audited here only.
edits.significanceNote: A conjecture from coding theory over near-rings, open since 1992 and formally stated in 2010, with a small literature that reduced it to a finite range in July 2026. Level with the Koizumi-Liu sign-alternation conjecture at 12, above a typical Erdos problem at 10 and Nathanson's product intersection problems at 8, below the multiplicative Merino-Welsh threshold at 14.

edits.name: Boshernitzan's Conjecture 2.2(e) for rational right and isosceles triangles
edits.statement: Let $\Delta$ be a rational triangle with angles $a\pi/d$, $b\pi/d$, $c\pi/d$ in lowest terms, placed with one side horizontal or vertical. Put $d'=\mathrm{lcm}(2,d)$ and $S^1(n)=\{z : z^n=1\}$, and let $P_0$ be the set of directions in which every billiard orbit that avoids the vertices is periodic (equivalently, the unfolded translation surface decomposes completely into cylinders). Boshernitzan proved that the rational exceptional directions of $\Delta$ lie in $S^1(2d')$ and stated Conjecture 2.2 in five parts. Part (e): if $\Delta$ is isosceles or a right triangle, then $S^1(2d')\subseteq P_0$. Computer searches of Delecroix and Rüth found counterexamples, among them the right triangle with angles $(4/15, 7/30, 1/2)\pi$ and the isosceles triangle $(7,7,16)\pi/30$, so (e) is false as stated. For which rational right and isosceles triangles does it hold?
edits.posedBy: M. D. Boshernitzan, Billiards and rational periodic directions in polygons, Amer. Math. Monthly 99 (1992), 522-529, Conjecture 2.2(e)
edits.ageNote: Posed in 1992; Boshernitzan checked parts (a) and (b) by computer for d at most 16. The sage-flatsurf census of Delecroix and Rüth (2022) refuted parts (a), (d) and (e): nine counterexamples to (a) with d at most 153, none to (b) with d at most 189. No proof covering an infinite family of non-lattice right triangles was known before this paper.
edits.aiRole: The paper's "Use of AI" section: "This paper - its text, its proofs and the code behind Appendices A and B, Proposition 6.4 and Theorem 6 - was drafted by an AI system (Claude, Anthropic) working under the author's direction, and checked by independent AI review passes and by the computations described in Appendices A and B, 6.3 and 9.2. The author has read parts of it in detail and takes responsibility for its content." Hexagon lists the tools as Anthropic Claude Opus, Python, SymPy and mpmath, and labels the work "Primarily AI-generated text; Human understanding: some parts".
edits.resultNote: Corollary 8.1: the right triangle with angles $(P, Q-P, Q)\pi/2Q$, $\gcd(P,Q)=1$, $\min(P,Q-P)\ge 2$, satisfies Conjecture 2.2(e) (both perpendicular direction classes completely periodic) when (1) $Q$ has at most one odd prime factor (computer-assisted in part); (2) $P\not\equiv \pm 2 \pmod p$ for every odd prime $p\mid Q$, a set of density about 0.62; (3), (4) two coding-theoretic families at composite $Q$; or (5) one of $P$, $Q-P$ is 4 and $Q\equiv 3 \pmod 4$ (interval arithmetic). At $Q\le 2000$ this covers 383,692 of 606,295 such triangles. Corollary 8.6 carries it to the isosceles triangles whose right halves are covered. The method cannot reach triangles where neither $P+2$ nor $P-2$ is a unit mod $Q$, where the known counterexample lies (Conjecture 6.5 covers the rest). Theorem 6 (computer-assisted): on three explicit intervals near 15/92, 21/242 and 23/270, every triangle $(a,2a,d-3a)\pi/d$ with $d$ even violates part (a), the first infinite family of counterexamples to (a).

edits.name: Whiteley's vertex splitting conjecture for generic global rigidity
edits.statement: A graph $G$ is generically globally rigid in $\mathbb{R}^d$ if, for a generic placement of its vertices in $\mathbb{R}^d$, the edge lengths determine the configuration up to isometry. A $d$-dimensional vertex split replaces a vertex $v$ by two adjacent vertices $v_1, v_2$ that share exactly $d-1$ of the neighbours of $v$ and divide the remaining neighbours between them. Whiteley proved that vertex splitting preserves generic rigidity in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and conjectured that it also preserves generic global rigidity in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whenever $v_1$ and $v_2$ both have degree at least $d+1$. Is this true in every dimension $d$?
edits.posedBy: W. Whiteley; stated as Conjecture 16 in R. Connelly and W. J. Whiteley, Global Rigidity: The Effect of Coning, Discrete Comput. Geom. 43 (2010), 717-735
edits.ageNote: Restated as Conjecture 1 by Jordan and Tanigawa (JCTB 2019), by Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa (DCG 2023, arXiv 2020) and in the 2026 Surveys in Combinatorics chapter on rigidity. The case $d=1$ is elementary and $d=2$ was proved by Jordan and Szabadka (2009); special cases for braced triangulations and simplicial circuits followed. Open for $d\ge 3$ before this paper.
edits.aiRole: The paper's "Statement on the use of artificial intelligence": "The proofs of all the new results in this paper were discovered by ChatGPT 6.1 Sol, which also produced the first draft of the paper. The author directed ChatGPT to investigate the problem and contributed to the revision of the manuscript to its current form. This included requesting clarifications and rewrites of the proofs, and making decisions about the organisation and presentation of the paper. The author has checked the arguments presented here and takes full responsibility for the paper."
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.2: if $uv\in E(G)$, $\deg_G(u),\deg_G(v)\ge d+1$, $|N_G(u)\cap N_G(v)|=d-1$, and $H=G/uv$ is generically globally rigid in $\mathbb{R}^d$, then so is $G$, for every $d\ge 1$. Corollary 1.5 allows at least $d-1$ common neighbours. Theorem 1.3 gives the stronger statement that $G$ is infinitesimally rigid at every generic realisation in which $u$ and $v$ coincide, which yields global rigidity through the Cruickshank-Jackson-Tanigawa coincident-rigidity criterion; two proofs, both via maximum-rank equilibrium stress matrices. Theorem 1.4 also proves the Jordan-Tanigawa conjecture (JCTB 2019, Conjecture 2) that every generically globally rigid graph has a nondegenerate equilibrium stress of maximum rank at every generic realisation.
edits.verificationNote: Read by this site on 15 November 2026. No independent mathematician has checked this yet; the author states that he checked the arguments. The conjecture's wording was compared with its restatement in Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa (arXiv 2002.08680), which attributes it to Whiteley via Connelly-Whiteley 2010 and Jordan-Tanigawa; the 2010 paper itself was not opened. Independent numerical check written here: 1,393 random vertex splits in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ of graphs on up to 10 vertices that pass a randomized Gortler-Healy-Thurston stress test for generic global rigidity; every split graph was infinitesimally rigid at a random realisation with the two split vertices coincident, as Theorem 1.3 predicts. The proofs were not checked.
edits.significanceNote: Whiteley's vertex splitting conjecture is a central open problem of combinatorial rigidity, restated in surveys and papers for over fifteen years, with the planar case and several graph classes proved. Famous within one community. Level with the tensor square conjecture for symmetric groups (28), below Saxl's conjecture (32), and well above the Garamvolgyi-Jackson-Jordan clique conjecture (8), a recent conjecture from the same school.

edits.name: Pak-Panova-Yeliussizov conjecture on Kronecker coefficients of Plancherel partitions
edits.statement:
For $\lambda\vdash n$ let $f^\lambda$ be the dimension of the irreducible representation $V^\lambda$ of $S_n$. A sequence of partitions $\lambda^{(n)}\vdash n$ is Plancherel if $f^{\lambda^{(n)}}\ge \sqrt{n!}\,e^{-a\sqrt n}$ for some fixed $a>0$. The Kronecker coefficient $g(\lambda,\mu,
u)$ is the multiplicity of $V^
u$ in $V^\lambda\otimes V^\mu$. Pak, Panova and Yeliussizov conjectured (Conjecture 3.10) that for any three Plancherel sequences, $g(\lambda^{(n)},\mu^{(n)},
u^{(n)})=\sqrt{n!}\,e^{-O(n)}$, and called the statement both plausible and out of reach. Is it true?
edits.posedBy: I. Pak, G. Panova and D. Yeliussizov, On the largest Kronecker and Littlewood-Richardson coefficients, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 165 (2019), 44-77 (arXiv 1804.04693), Conjecture 3.10

edits.name: Rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics for colorings of $G(n,d/n)$ in the uniqueness regime
edits.statement: Let $G\sim G(n,d/n)$ be a sparse Erdős-Rényi random graph with fixed average degree $d$. Is the single-site Glauber dynamics on proper $q$-colorings of $G$ rapidly mixing, with high probability over $G$, for every $q$ in the tree uniqueness regime, that is for $q\ge d+2$? Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic and Vigoda record this as the prediction from statistical physics (Krzakala et al.) and proved rapid mixing for $q>\alpha d$, $\alpha\approx1.7632$, for large $d$.
edits.posedBy: Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic and Vigoda, recording a prediction of Krzakala, Montanari, Ricci-Tersenghi, Semerjian and Zdeborova (2007)
edits.ageNote: The uniqueness-regime prediction is attributed to Krzakala et al., PNAS 2007, a physics paper; the explicit statement for Glauber dynamics on G(n,d/n) with q at least d+2 is in Efthymiou-Hayes-Stefankovic-Vigoda, arXiv 1707.03796 (SODA 2018). Mossel-Sly (2010) and Efthymiou (2014) had earlier bounds.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$, all sufficiently large $d$ and all integers $q\ge d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, with probability $1-o(1)$ over $G\sim G(n,d/n)$ the Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings has $\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}(\delta)=O_{d,\varepsilon}\big(n^{2+\zeta}(1+\log(1/\delta))\big)$ with $\zeta=C_\varepsilon\log q/d^{\varepsilon}$. This improves $q>1.763d$ (EHSV 2018). Three weeks earlier Li and Yang (arXiv 2610.25391, also AI-assisted) proved polynomial mixing for $q\ge(1+o_d(1))d$; the present paper gives an explicit surplus $d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ and a near-quadratic mixing time. Partial: large $d$ only, and $q=d+2$ is not reached.
edits.aiRole: From the paper's AI disclosure (Section 1.4): the main ideas of the proofs were developed using long interactions with GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6.1 Sol, after instructing it to devise a Bochner-type inequality for block dynamics for proper colorings. The same models assisted with writing. The author states that all claims and calculations were independently verified by him and takes full responsibility.
edits.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Li and Yang (arXiv 2610.25391, 18 October 2026) had already proved rapid mixing for q at least (1+o(1))d, also with GPT models disclosed; the author calls the two works concurrent and independent, and this one is quantitatively stronger. edits.name: Smale's mean value constant: is it exactly 4?
edits.statement: For a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d\ge 2$ with $p(0)=0$ and $p'(0)\ne 0$, let $S(p)=\min_{p'(c)=0}|p(c)/(c\,p'(0))|$, and let $K(d)$ be the supremum of $S(p)$ over all such $p$ of degree $d$. Smale (1981) proved $K(d)\le 4$ for every $d$ and asked whether $4$ can be replaced by $1$; that was disproved in 2026. What is the exact value of Smale's mean value constant $K^*=\sup_{d\ge2}K(d)$? Jatar and Ng (2026) list whether $K^*=4$ as open.
edits.posedBy: Stephen Smale; the exact value restated as open by Aneesh Jatar and Tuen-Wai Ng (2026)
edits.ageNote: Smale asked for the best constant in 1981 and conjectured 1. After the 2026 disproof of K=1, Jatar and Ng (arXiv 2610.21472, Section 9) proved K* > 1.1018 and wrote that whether K* = 4 is open; Goel then claimed K* > 1.1559.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: $K^*=\lim_{d\to\infty}K(d)=4$. Each $K(d)$ is known to be below $4$, so the supremum is not attained, and the proof gives no bound on the degree needed to exceed a given $a<4$. The proof combines the Jatar-Ng reduction to admissible univalent-Blaschke pairs with an explicit construction. Lean: Smale.P030.Rows.thm_1_1 (and kstar_eq_four, tendsto_Kd_four) at tag v2.50. This answers the exact-value question; the $K=1$ conjecture was disproved earlier (see the related entry).

edits.significanceNote: This is Smale's 1981 problem itself: the best constant in his mean value theorem, on his list for the twenty-first century, with forty-five years of work lowering the bound toward 1. The K = 1 disproof answered the yes-or-no form; the exact value is the question that then remained. edits.name: Talagrand's Ultimate Matching Conjecture
edits.field: probability theory, random matching, optimal transport
edits.statement: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ be independent uniform points in $[0,1]^2$ and let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_N$ be evenly spread (each in its own rectangle of area $1/N$ and diameter $O(1/\sqrt{N})$). Talagrand's Ultimate Matching Conjecture (Research Problem 17.1.2 of his 2021 monograph) asks: for exponents $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\ge 2$ with $1/\alpha_1+1/\alpha_2=1/2$, is there a constant $L$ such that with high probability one permutation $\pi$ satisfies $\sum_{i}\exp\big[\big(\sqrt{N}|X_i^j-Y_{\pi(i)}^j|/(L\sqrt{\log N})\big)^{\alpha_j}\big]\le 2N$ for both coordinates $j=1,2$, with $\alpha_j=\infty$ read as $\max_i|X_i^j-Y_{\pi(i)}^j|\le L\sqrt{\log N/N}$?
edits.posedBy: Michel Talagrand
edits.ageNote: The source cites Research Problem 17.1.2, equation (17.3), of Talagrand's Upper and Lower Bounds for Stochastic Processes, 2nd ed. (Springer, 2021). Whether the same conjecture already appears in the 2014 first edition was not checked here.
edits.aiRole: Per the paper's 'Use of AI tools' section and the Hexagon provenance statement: several weeks of interaction with LLMs produced a first proof in the subcritical case; a later round produced the critical finite-exponent case (finite-exponents.pdf in the GitHub repository), and GPT-6 then obtained the endpoint asymptotics (endpoints.pdf). The Hexagon manuscript itself was mostly generated and proof-checked by LLMs while the authors worked to understand those versions; the authors say they have an overall understanding and plan a fully digested version. Hexagon lists OpenAI ChatGPT and Anthropic Claude Fable as tools.
edits.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here on 15 November 2026: the Hexagon PDF (2611.00294v1, dated 10 November 2026, three named authors at CNRS/Universite Gustave Eiffel and Pisa) and its abstract page; Theorem 1.1, Definition 10.1 and Theorem 20.1 read against the paper's own restatement of Research Problem 17.1.2 (Talagrand's book itself was not opened); the AI disclosure is in the paper and on the Hexagon page, which labels the text 'Primarily AI-generated' with 'Human understanding: some parts'; the GitHub repository README lists the undigested AI-generated derivations. The proof (about 70 pages) was not checked. Hexagon is a moderated but not peer-reviewed repository; acceptance there is not a judgement of correctness.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for finite $\alpha_1,\alpha_2>2$ with $1/\alpha_1+1/\alpha_2=1/2$ (including the quartic case $(4,4)$), with probability tending to one a single permutation satisfies the conjectured bound in both coordinates, for an evenly spread deterministic configuration and also for two independent samples; subcritical exponents follow. Theorem 20.1: at the hard endpoints $(2,\infty)$ and $(\infty,2)$ the normalized optimal matching cost diverges in probability, so the conjecture fails there. The paper thus answers the conjecture in every case: true for finite critical exponents, false at the endpoints. Exact endpoint asymptotics are claimed only in the repository's endpoints.pdf, not in the paper.
edits.significanceNote: A named research problem in Talagrand's own monograph, the endpoint of the Ajtai-Komlos-Tusnady matching line that his chaining and majorizing-measure work organized, and a problem he singled out in his favorite-problems writing. Known widely in probability, not far beyond. Placed level with the Erdos similarity geometric-progression entry (34) and just above Talagrand's operator cotype problem (32), which comes from the same book but is narrower; below Sogge's local smoothing (72).

edits.name: Castro-Silva's conjecture: large triangles in planar sets of positive upper density
edits.statement: Conjecture 1 of Castro-Silva: let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be a measurable set of positive upper density, $\limsup_{T\to\infty}|A\cap[-T,T]^2|/(2T)^2>0$, and let $u,v,w\in\mathbb{R}^2$ be non-collinear points. Is there $t_0>0$ such that for every $t\ge t_0$ the set $A$ contains a configuration congruent to $\{tu,tv,tw\}$?
edits.posedBy: Davi Castro-Silva
edits.ageNote: Conjecture 1 of Castro-Silva, Geometrical sets with forbidden configurations, arXiv 2102.10018 (v1 February 2021; Forum Math. Sigma 11, 2023). He calls it the simplest case of his conjecture and 'an obvious question left open since the results of Bourgain and of Furstenberg, Katznelson and Weiss' (1986 and 1990); Bourgain's simplex theorem covers triangles only in dimension at least three.

The repository at that commit (19 Lean files, about 29,000 lines) was grepped: no sorry outside the challenge stub, no axiom, native_decide, unsafe or implemented_by. Not rebuilt here. The challenge statement was written by the formalizing model and checked by the author, so it is not independently anchored.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if $\Delta\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is three noncollinear points and $E\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is measurable with upper Banach density $d^*(E)>0$, there is $\lambda_0$ such that for every $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$ the set $E$ contains a translate of a rotation of $\lambda\Delta$. Since upper Banach density dominates the centred upper density and rotated translates are congruent copies, this gives Castro-Silva's Conjecture 1 in full, in a stronger orientation-preserving form. Castro-Silva's broader conjecture for $d+1$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ in other dimensions is not addressed. Earlier: Falconer, Kovac and Yavicoli (2022) for $d^*(E)>1/2$; Furstenberg, Katznelson and Weiss for neighbourhoods of $E$.
edits.significanceNote: The planar triangle case of Bourgain's simplex theorem, the obvious gap left since Bourgain (1986) and Furstenberg, Katznelson and Weiss: well known in Euclidean Ramsey theory and harmonic analysis, with Falconer-Kovac-Yavicoli reaching density above one half. Placed above the Leader-Russell-Walters Euclidean Ramsey entry (28), which is narrower, and level with the Erdos similarity geometric-progression entry (34) and the HRT conjecture (33).
